There’s quite a bit! It certainly wouldn’t be wise to plan a wedding without some sort of planning experience, though it’d still be great if you could help out anyway you can. I think the most you could realistically get into right now would be looking into things in this order:

1. Choose a vendor (DJ, florist, photographer, etc.)
2. Choose an approximate budget
3. Decide on a date and venue
4. Decide on menu items
5. Create a guest list
6. Decide on décor and decor elements (candles, flowers, etc.)
7. Choose a dress, and set a date to try it on and try out different looks
8. Decide if you’d like a first dance or a first kissing ritual
9. Decide on a ceremony music selection
10. Plan and order your wedding invitations

Climate Prediction Center's guide to El Niño conditions
El Niño is the warming of waters in the eastern tropical Pacific. Normally, these waters are cool. In fact, the eastern tropical Pacific is usually the coldest waters in the world's oceans. This "cold pool" allows the air above it to rise and get removed from the atmosphere as the trade winds move the air westward toward the Americas. This rise in the air allows the Pacific Ocean to spill more water into the Gulf of Alaska. If the temperature of the waters in the eastern tropical Pacific warms, then the trade winds decrease. The result is that more moisture is released into the atmosphere and the Pacific will "short circuit" the air mass of the world. This means that when the air mass moves westward from the Pacific, it cannot pass over the western part of North America. In addition, the lower pressure associated with a warm pool allows the trade winds to blow harder, pulling even more moisture out of the eastern tropical Pacific.

Lasagna can really add a nice touch to a party.  Perhaps not as much as pasta salad or meatloaf, or such, but I think lasagna would be nice with some company.  If you can make it, it should be a nice challenge.  Feel free to ask more about how to prepare it, etc.  It is quite easy to make, if not the best known recipe goes like this.  

Ingredients:

2 cups all-purpose flour  

2 tsp salt  

1 tsp sugar  

2 large baking potatoes, peeled and chopped  

3/4 cup margarine

Directions:

Preheat your oven to 350 degrees.  

Put the whole potatoes in a large pot of salted boiling water and cook until just tender, about 15 minutes.  Drain, mash with a mixer and mix in the margarine and flour.  Spread in a greased 9x13 inch pan and bake for 20 minutes.  Allow to cool and then cut into squares.  You now have the lasagna noodles.  

In a separate bowl mix together the flour and salt.  Cut in the margarine with a pastry blender or two knives.  Add the 3/4 cup water and mix just until the dough forms a ball.  Form into a ball and place in refrigerator for 1 hour to chill.  

After the 1 hour has elapsed, take your dough out of the refrigerator and place on a floured surface.  Cover and let rest for 1 hour.  In a separate bowl mix together milk, egg, salt and pepper.  

When the lasagna dough has rested, punch it down.  Cut it into lasagna noodles.  Add 2 cups of your sauce of choice in the bottom of a large casserole dish, then add a layer of noodles, then a layer of your desired cheese and then another layer of noodles.  The remaining ingredients can be added in this order: tomato sauce, more cheese, more noodles, meat sauce, more noodles, broccoli, meatloaf, more noodles, more cheese.  

Cover tightly and bake at 350 degrees for 35-45 minutes or until bubbly.  Allow to rest for 5 minutes before serving.  

If too much sauce or cheese is used you can skip it for the next layer and put ricotta, parmesan or mozzarella on top instead.  

This recipe yields about twenty servings.   You can make it ahead of time, up to that stage.   Cover and refrigerate up to that point.   But then bake right before serving.
